item.title: TechCentral’s International Newsmakers of 2025
item.description: This is TechCentral's list of the top international newsmakers in the tech industry in 2025, a year that was shaped by geopolitics.

item.title: Telecoms industry backs Malatsi policy directive, warns on execution
item.description: ACT has welcomed communications minister Solly Malatsi's policy directive to Icasa on BEE.

item.title: Crypto’s Trump-era boom faces a 2026 reality check
item.description: It has been a year of policy victories, but crypto firms warn momentum could fade without durable US legislation.

item.title: Coursera to buy Udemy, in which Prosus is an investor
item.description: Coursera will acquire rival Udemy in an all-stock deal, valuing the combined company at $2.5-billion.

item.title: China races to crack EUV lithography as chip war with the West intensifies
item.description: China’s new EUV prototype signals a faster path to semiconductor self-sufficiency, challenging Western chip-making dominance.

item.title: Malatsi buries Post Office monopoly the market ignored
item.description: Government has scrapped the Post Office’s sub-1kg parcel monopoly, finally aligning the law with market reality.

item.title: TechCentral’s South African Newsmakers of 2025
item.description: TechCentral's South African Newsmakers of 2025 are people who shaped outcomes that reached beyond boardrooms.

item.title: Trump space order puts the moon back at centre of US, China rivalry
item.description: US President Donald Trump has ordered a 2028 moon landing, refocusing Nasa’s priorities amid growing competition with China.

item.title: Starlink satellite anomaly creates debris in rare orbital mishap
item.description: A Starlink satellite has suffered a rare orbital anomaly, shedding debris and highlighting growing risks in Earth’s orbit.

item.title: Digital authoritarianism grows as African states normalise internet blackouts
item.description: Internet shutdowns are increasing dramatically across the Africa continent – a new book explains why.
